title: Fixation Hold with Peripheral Flash
summary: A fixation-hold task in which, on half of the trials, a brief peripheral flash appears 8 dva left or right of fixation. The subject must maintain fixation throughout. The experiment measures the rate and latency of fixation breaks on flash versus no-flash trials.
paradigm: Each trial begins with the subject acquiring fixation on a central point. After a stable hold, a brief peripheral flash appears on half the trials, either 8 dva left or right of fixation; on the other half, no flash occurs. The subject must keep their gaze on the fixation point throughout. Conditions (flash left, flash right, no flash) are served equally, in sequence or shuffled, with each condition repeated the configured number of times.

design.label: Conditions
design.value: Flash left, Flash right, No flash

design.label: Session length
design.value: 5–15 minutes, depending on subject and n_per_condition

stimuli.name: fixation
stimuli.notes: White fixation point at screen center.

stimuli.name: flash
stimuli.position: 8 dva left or right of fixation
stimuli.notes: Brief white disk, appears only on flash trials. Size is conventional.

measures.name: outcome
measures.definition: Whether fixation was held throughout the trial (FIXATED), broken during or after the flash (FIX_BREAK), or never acquired (NO_FIXATION).

measures.name: fixation_break_latency_ms
measures.definition: Time from flash onset to fixation break, on trials where fixation is broken after the flash.

measures.name: acquire_latency_ms
measures.definition: Time from trial start to fixation acquired.

parameters.meaning: Diameter of the central fixation point.

parameters.name: acquire_timeout
parameters.label: Fixation acquire timeout

parameters.meaning: Duration to hold fixation before the flash or equivalent point on no-flash trials.

parameters.name: flash_duration

parameters.name: flash_eccentricity_dva

timeline.until: Gaze enters fixation window or timeout elapses
timeline.note: Wait for gaze to enter fixation region; ends early if acquired.
Subject must hold fixation for configured duration before flash or equivalent point.
Peripheral flash appears for flash trials only; skipped on no-flash trials.

timeline.until: Fixation is broken or flash_duration elapses (for flash trials), or equivalent time passes (no-flash trials)
timeline.note: Monitor for fixation break after flash; record latency if break occurs.

tasks.name: fixation-flash
tasks.description: Fixation-hold task with a brief peripheral flash on half the trials, measuring fixation breaks and their latency.

tests.name: Parameters load
tests.how: Load the parameters file and check all required fields are present and valid.

tests.name: Timeline and outcomes
tests.how: Run a simulated trial for each condition and check the timeline phases and possible outcomes.

tests.name: Condition counts
tests.how: Check that each condition is served paradigm.n_per_condition times.

tests.name: Simulated trial
tests.how: Run a simulated session with alhazen's fakes and verify that fixation is held or broken as expected, and that latencies are recorded.

notes: Flash size (1.0 dva), flash duration (50 ms), and flash eccentricity (8 dva) are conventional values chosen for peripheral flash visibility. No-flash trials are included as a third condition. Inter-trial interval (500 ms), pre-flash hold (500 ms), and fixation window (2.0 dva) are standard. The post-flash hold phase is event-driven to allow measurement of fixation break latency. The flash appears left or right with equal probability; both are explicit conditions.
